target_customer: Urban consumers in Addis Ababa ordering food, groceries, parcels and pharmacy items, plus restaurants and merchants as partners
problem: Food delivery in Ethiopia was expensive and fragmented. beU offers cheap door to door delivery from local restaurants.
business_model: Marketplace take rate plus delivery fees on orders, with rider network and merchant partners
product_category: On-demand food and goods delivery app

founders.name: Hao Zheng
education: University of California San Diego, double major in Mathematics and Chemistry (honors)
Johns Hopkins University, master's in Bioinformatics, dropped out midway to start a company
founders.background_notes: YC page says he did liver, head and neck research and authored eight peer-reviewed publications.

competitors.name: Deliver Addis
competitors.what: Local Ethiopian food delivery startup that dominated Addis Ababa before beU entered
competitors.traction_then: Market leader per beU's founder; beU later claimed to pass it by 20 percent share within eight months

competitors.name: Uber Eats
competitors.what: Global platform named by EqualOcean as displaced by beU in local takeaway

technical_complexity.rationale: Standard delivery marketplace app with dispatch and rider logistics, with operations harder than software.

defensibility.rationale: Local density of riders and restaurants helps, but six to seven delivery firms already operated and low prices were the main lever.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found. beU reported becoming the largest Ethiopian food delivery provider, expanded to e-commerce, and per Shega had its first profitable month in May 2025.

market_need_then: EqualOcean says six to seven food delivery companies already operated, and beU founder said it undercut them on price. Growing smartphone use in Addis Ababa supported demand.

branding.name_origin: Loline Magazine says the name conveys self-expression and that its country director admits it seems unrelated to the delivery business, the vision being a super app.

identity.visual_style: Orange rider uniforms mentioned in search summaries of press, local and homegrown feel
identity.voice_and_tone: Friendly, approachable, short and direct copy with emojis, tagline 'We Deliver Convenience'

branding.brand_signature: Orange uniformed delivery riders (reported by press, not confirmed by an opened page)

brand_strength.rationale: Reported market leader with distinctive rider look and local identity, but evidence on the brand itself is thin.

pivots.from: Social app started in China in 2019
pivots.why: Per EqualOcean the company began as a social app in China and entered food delivery in Ethiopia in June 2021.

outcome_analysis: beU entered Addis Ababa in June 2021 with low prices and grew to be called the largest food delivery provider in Ethiopia, with about 300 staff, 3M deliveries and a first profitable month in May 2025 per Shega after roughly $4M invested. It remains active and has added grocery, pharmacy and e-commerce. Funding totals are poorly documented.
notes: Seed reported as 'millions of USD' led by Y Combinator (EqualOcean, Pandaily) with no amount, so amount is null. Single outlet Shega reports $300K from MiraclePlus (Fall 2022), unverified. Total raised conflicts: $860K (CB Insights), about $2.5M (Dealroom), $4M invested per Shega 2025, and Latka says bootstrapped. Loline Magazine names Almas Beleshov and Matt Artemovich as co-founders with Hao Zheng; YC page lists only Zheng, so they are not recorded as founders. Wan site says product of Binary Technologies. Shega lists Zmall and others as 2024 era rivals; Zmall dating near batch is only a 2021 award note.
